_readme: Twenty realistic decide() calls used as an eval set by scripts/test-decide.mjs, alongside the full-grid property test. Every `expected` was drafted by RUNNING decide() against the live catalog and reading real fields off the winning models (see each rationale) — never from opinion about which model 'should' win. That also means this file is a trip-wire on purpose: if a future data refresh changes prices, scores, or availability enough to flip one of these, the eval fails loud (see the 'Derive task fit' + test step in .github/workflows/auto-refresh.yml) rather than silently drifting. start_here_any_of: [] means the situation is expected to return an EMPTY shortlist (nothing clears every filter) — test-decide.mjs treats that as its own assertion, not 'any model is fine'. Where the underlying data is thin enough that a refresh could plausibly reorder close scores, start_here_any_of lists more than one acceptable id and the rationale says so.

situations.description: Solo developer, OpenRouter only, cheap high-volume batch job.
situations.rationale: Llama 4 Maverick is the cheapest OpenRouter-reachable model with a general score (GPQA) to weight against price ($0.22/$0.88). Qwen3 Max has no sourced GPQA or MMLU-Pro, so bulk's floor (a general-capability basis) excludes it even though it's reachable and cheap.

situations.description: Enterprise team paying for Anthropic only, balanced coding pick.
situations.rationale: Balanced blends normalized coding_score with normalized price; Claude Sonnet 5 (coding_score 85, $19/mo at typical volume) sits between Haiku's cheap-but-weaker and Opus's strongest-but-priciest. OpenAI and Google models are unreachable — 'have' names Anthropic only.

situations.description: CTO wants the strongest researcher, any vendor, no China-hosted models.
situations.rationale: Gemini 3.1 Pro has the highest research fit (GPQA 94.3 + 1M context) among non-China-hosted models. DeepSeek (China) and Moonshot AI / Kimi (China) both carry strong GPQA scores that would otherwise be competitive — data/vendors.json marks both China-headquartered, so noChinaHosted must drop them regardless of score.

situations.description: Marketing team on an OpenAI plan, balanced pick for long-form copy.
situations.rationale: Writing fit is GPQA-or-MMLU-Pro as-is; among reachable OpenAI models GPT-5.6 Luna's balance of a high GPQA (91.6) at $1.2/$2.16-per-1M-tokens pricing wins the blended rank. Claude Opus 5 is unreachable — 'have' names OpenAI only.

situations.description: Small startup, any vendor, cheapest extraction pipeline at light volume.
situations.rationale: Same floor gap as the bulk case: extraction needs a general score AND a price. Llama 4 Maverick has both and is the cheapest to clear; Qwen3 Max has no sourced GPQA/MMLU-Pro so it never clears the floor no matter how cheap it is.

situations.description: Customer-support bot builder with a Google-only budget, cheapest chat model.
situations.rationale: Gemini 3.5 Flash is the only reachable Google model that clears chat's floor (a sourced general score) once dominated candidates are dropped. GPT-5.6 Luna is unreachable — 'have' names Google only.

situations.description: Frontend developer with xAI access only, wants the strongest option.
situations.rationale: Grok 4.5 has a sourced coding_score (86); frontend fit is coding_score plus a small best_for:speed bonus. Grok 4.6 has neither a sourced coding_score nor a sourced direct_api flag yet, so it fails both the floor and (separately) reachability.

situations.description: Analyst on Anthropic, heavy volume, balanced pick for executive summaries.
situations.rationale: exec-summaries fit is the general score as-is; Claude Sonnet 5 has a sourced GPQA where Claude Haiku 4.5 does not, so Haiku fails the floor entirely despite being the cheapest Anthropic model — a same-vendor case showing the floor is about sourced capability, not just reachability.

situations.description: Screenshot/QA tool, any vendor, cheapest model that actually handles images.
situations.rationale: Vision fit is a plain yes/no on the best_for:vision tag; every tagged model ties at 100, so the cheapest one (Inkling Small) dominates the rest of the tie and is the only survivor. Claude Opus 5 carries no vision tag in this data, so it's excluded regardless of how capable it may actually be — an unsourced fact stays null, never a guessed yes.

situations.description: OpenRouter-only builder, balanced coding pick, no China-hosted models.
situations.rationale: The single strongest coding_score reachable via OpenRouter is actually Kimi K3 (96, Moonshot AI) — which is exactly why this case matters: data/vendors.json marks Moonshot AI and DeepSeek China-headquartered, so noChinaHosted must drop both regardless of how high they score, leaving GPT-5.6 Luna's balanced price/capability trade-off on top.

situations.description: Automation builder with xAI access only, strongest agentic pick.
situations.rationale: Updated 2026-09-07 (engine round 3, judged task fit): Grok 4.6 now carries a sourced judged-fit record for agents (xAI's own launch post, matching GPT-5.6 Sol on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index) — a real basis where before there was none. At the same price as Grok 4.5 ($2/$6) but a higher fit (88 judged vs. 72 measured), it strictly dominates Grok 4.5, which drops from the shortlist entirely rather than merely losing the top spot.

situations.description: Compliance-sensitive team, Google only, no-China rule (belt-and-suspenders), extraction.
situations.rationale: Google's own HQ is the United States, so noChinaHosted doesn't change this set — the interesting part is that Gemini 3.1 Pro, despite a strong GPQA, is dropped as dominated (Gemini 3.5 Flash is both cheaper and has an equal-or-better blended extraction fit), leaving one survivor.

situations.description: Budget chat app, OpenRouter only, cheapest that clears the floor.
situations.rationale: Same general-score gap again: Llama 4 Maverick is the cheapest OpenRouter model with a sourced general score; Qwen3 Max has none, so it never clears chat's floor.

situations.description: Research lab, any vendor, no-China rule, strongest researcher at heavy volume.
situations.rationale: Fit ranking (rule 4) doesn't depend on volume — only the displayed monthly_cost_usd does — so this repeats the CTO case's winner at a different cost figure. DeepSeek's GPQA (90.1) would otherwise be in range, but it's China-headquartered.

situations.description: Enterprise paying for both Anthropic and OpenAI, balanced coding at heavy volume.
situations.rationale: With two vendors reachable, GPT-5.6 Luna's cheap-but-decent coding_score wins the balanced blend over Anthropic's pricier options at heavy volume. Google is unreachable — 'have' names Anthropic and OpenAI only, not Google.

situations.description: Freelancer on OpenRouter, balanced pick for a vision task.
situations.rationale: Same tie-and-price-dominate pattern as the vision-cheapest case: every vision-tagged, OpenRouter-reachable model ties at fit 100, and Inkling Small is the cheapest of them, so it's the sole survivor under any price-sensitive stance. Claude Opus 5 has no vision tag in this data.

situations.description: Freelancer on OpenRouter, cheapest extraction pick at light volume.
situations.rationale: Identical floor logic to the other extraction/bulk/chat cases at a different volume — volume changes monthly_cost_usd, not which models clear the general-score floor or which is cheapest per token.

situations.description: Solo builder on Anthropic only, cheapest frontend-capable model.
situations.rationale: Claude Haiku 4.5 has a sourced coding_score (66) and is the cheapest Anthropic model that clears frontend's floor. GPT-5.6 Luna is unreachable — 'have' names Anthropic only.

situations.description: Edge case: caller has no vendor access at all.
situations.rationale: An empty `have` matches nothing under rule 1 (it isn't 'any') — every model is unreachable, so the shortlist must be empty. This is the edge case for 'have provided but grants nothing', distinct from 'any' meaning no filter.

situations.description: Edge case: the only vendor the caller has doesn't publish a vision-capable model in this data.
situations.rationale: No Anthropic model carries a 'vision' best_for tag in this snapshot, so every Anthropic model fails vision's floor and the shortlist is empty — this is a floor failure, not a reachability failure (Anthropic models ARE reachable here for other tasks).
